lead: >-
  On longer itineraries through Bolivia, Peru and Uruguay, the most active adventure takes place in Bolivia's highlands: a 4×4 journey through lagoons and salt flats. Peru adds Lake Titicaca, the road from Puno to Cusco and an excursion to Machu Picchu, while Uruguay offers a one-day trip to Montevideo. It is a busy journey with complex transport and altitude considerations, but the confirmed programme is not a multi-day trek through all three countries.
---

## What kind of adventure awaits in these three countries?

Our [Bolivia, Peru and Uruguay selection](/multi-country/bolivia_peru_uruguay/) features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} including these main countries and the Adventure theme. Both itineraries extend far beyond the three named countries. Evaluate them primarily by the demands involved: long drives, high altitude, changes of transport and the density of sightseeing days.

**The principal active stage is the jeep journey in [Bolivia](/bolivia/).** From San Pedro de Atacama, travellers cross into the Bolivian Altiplano and travel by four-wheel drive past [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), the Salvador Dalí Desert, Sol de Mañana geysers and [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). They then continue through high-altitude lagoons towards [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). The adventure involves off-road driving, stops at natural sites and high-altitude conditions.

In [Peru](/peru/), the activities differ: a border crossing at Desaguadero, a visit to [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), a tourist-bus journey to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) with stops, an excursion to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and walks among archaeological monuments. There is time to explore on foot, but the itineraries do not list a self-guided, multi-day Inca Trail hike.

[Uruguay](/uruguay/) is visited by ferry from Buenos Aires to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) and back on the same day. This city excursion adds variety to the expedition experiences but does not include a safari, trek or extreme water sport.

## Two days by off-road vehicle: why this is a distinct stage

Bolivia's jeep section demands more attention than an ordinary city tour. First, travellers see turquoise Laguna Verde and volcanic landscapes near the Chilean border. Polques hot springs, Sol de Mañana geysers and reddish Laguna Colorada follow. The tours include an overnight stay in expedition-style accommodation on the highlands.

The next stage brings Honda, Chiar Khota, Hedionda and Cañapa lagoons, Ollagüe Volcano, Chiguana Salt Flat and the vast white surface of Uyuni. Near Colchani, visitors learn about salt processing and stop at other sites on the salt flat. The time available for photographs depends on light, weather and road conditions.

Driving by jeep is not equivalent to a difficult hiking expedition. The main requirements are tolerance of the road, altitude, wind and changing temperatures. Ordinary city shoes may suffice for a short sightseeing stop, but stable soles are more practical on dusty, uneven and cold ground. Check the exact vehicles, accommodation and stops included in your tour.

Those particularly interested in nature-based off-road travel can compare [adventure tours in Bolivia](/interests/adventure/tours/bolivia/) by the duration of their active stages, rather than country counts alone.

## Peru: Andean heritage without an invented trek

After [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/), the route passes through [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/) towards Peru. This day combines heritage sightseeing and an international land crossing. The afternoon programme includes the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/) on Titicaca. The next major drive is by tourist bus, through villages and La Raya Pass to Cusco.

Machu Picchu has a dedicated excursion day. The programme includes a train journey and a guided group visit to the archaeological complex, followed by a return trip by rail. This does **not** imply an included Inca Trail trek or an ascent of nearby summits. Visitors need comfortable footwear for steps and walking within the complex, but the exact walking requirements depend on the ticket's permitted circuit and current rules.

The Peru section combines a high-altitude lake, settlements, an Andean crossing, the former Inca capital and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). If a long mountain trek is your priority, choose a separate product explicitly describing its route. Check [adventure tours in Peru](/interests/adventure/tours/peru/) for such differences within individual itineraries.

## Comparing the 20-day and 32-day journeys

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_latin_america_six_countries_20_days_2026,tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

The [20-day Six Latin American Countries tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) connects Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and Peru. Its itinerary moves from Rio and Iguazu towards the Pacific and Andean regions. The jeep section, Titicaca, Cusco and Machu Picchu occupy a busy second half.

The [32-day Eight South American Countries journey](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) adds Ecuador and Colombia after Peru. Ecuador includes the Galápagos with a sea excursion day, while Colombia features Guatapé, Medellín, Cartagena and Bogotá. This adds substantial travel and many days away from home, although the principal Bolivia–Peru–Uruguay jeep and heritage stages remain comparable.

If you mainly want off-road travel and highland scenery, first decide how many days you want to spend specifically in Bolivia and Peru, then whether the additional countries are worth the travel time. You can also compare [multi-country Adventure tours](/multi-country/interests/adventure/) beyond this three-country selection.

## Altitude, wellbeing and border preparations

Sections of the Bolivian route exceed 4,000 metres. Later, the road through Peru's La Raya Pass also reaches around 4,400 metres. Overnight stays in La Paz and Cusco form part of the high-altitude journey. The risk of altitude sickness does not depend solely on fitness: the pace of ascent, prior acclimatisation, wellbeing and individual factors all matter. Discuss medical advice, medicines and contraindications with a doctor before travelling.

Daily routines change several times. Bolivia features early departures and hours on rough roads; Peru involves sightseeing, a tourist-bus crossing of the Andes and the railway to Machu Picchu; Uruguay involves a ferry and a city walk. Pack warm windproof layers for the Altiplano and lighter clothes for city days. Sun protection is needed even in cold, high-altitude conditions.

Before the Bolivia–Peru border crossing and the Argentina–Uruguay day trip, check passport and entry requirements for each nationality, including re-entry and transit conditions. Each country has its own currency and payment infrastructure, so arrange payment methods, card acceptance, currency exchange and cash reserves beforehand. Flights, ferry journeys and the land crossing must form a single coordinated schedule with sufficient buffers.

Ada Tours can coordinate the transport stages and explain which active days are actually included. If you want additional trekking or another adventure format, its availability and timing must be established before redesigning the individual itinerary.

## Frequently asked questions about adventures in Bolivia, Peru and Uruguay

### Do I need to be an experienced mountaineer?

No technical ascent is listed in these programmes. Nonetheless, altitude, long vehicle journeys and walking excursions call for preparation and an assessment of health. The absence of mountaineering does not mean the journey is physically effortless.

### Is the Inca Trail trek to Machu Picchu included?

No. The itinerary specifies a one-day excursion from Cusco to Machu Picchu with a return by rail. Mountain trekking requires a separately confirmed product with its own terms.

### Is visiting Montevideo an adventure excursion?

No. Uruguay is visited on a one-day city excursion from Buenos Aires, involving a ferry and capital-city sightseeing. The active off-road stage takes place in Bolivia.

### How long is the jeep section itself?

The itineraries allocate two consecutive days: first the high-altitude lagoons and volcanic features, then more lakes, salt flats and Uyuni. On the full tour, these days are surrounded by flights, excursions and transfers.

### Is the 32-day tour suitable if I only want the Altiplano?

It suits travellers who also want Ecuador, Colombia and other South American countries. For a journey focused on the Altiplano, discuss a separate route without unnecessary long-distance flights.

buttonLabel: "History and culture in Bolivia, Peru and Uruguay"
lead: >-
  Bolivia, Peru and Uruguay offer three distinct historical narratives on one journey: the pre-Inca civilisation of Tiwanaku on the Altiplano, Inca heritage in Cusco and Machu Picchu, and Montevideo's colonial urban history. On two existing extended itineraries, these stops are interspersed with flights, high-altitude transfers and nature excursions. Compare the monuments, cultural days and differences between the 20-day and 32-day journeys.
---

## Three countries and three historical periods

Our themed selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} that include [Bolivia](/bolivia/), [Peru](/peru/) and [Uruguay](/uruguay/) as principal countries. Their history programmes are not distributed equally: the more substantial archaeological experiences are in Bolivia and Peru, whereas Uruguay is a day trip to its capital.

In Bolivia, the cultural stage begins in [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) with historic districts and the Witches' Market, followed by [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/) on the way to the Peruvian border. Travellers encounter traces of a society that predated the Inca Empire, then continue into Peru's Andean heritage.

In Peru, historic sites follow one another: the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/) on [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), stops on the tourist-bus route from Puno to Cusco, [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) itself, [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and Sacred Valley monuments in the surrounding region. Some stops occur during travel days, while Machu Picchu has a separate excursion day.

In Uruguay, the historical focus is [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/): its port, Independence Square, Old Town and cathedral. It introduces a South American capital from a different era. No archaeological excavations relating to Tiwanaku or the Inca are included or advertised in Uruguay.

## Tiwanaku: Bolivia's pre-Inca history

Tiwanaku stands on Bolivia's high-altitude plateau. UNESCO lists it as World Heritage, recognising the political and spiritual centre of a pre-Columbian civilisation that developed before the flourishing of the Inca state. Visitors can see monumental stonework, ceremonial spaces, the Gate of the Sun and Kalasasaya Temple.

Both itineraries include Tiwanaku during the drive from La Paz towards Desaguadero and Puno. It is not a separate multi-day archaeological expedition. The visit is scheduled for the stated sights; a comprehensive academic course covering all excavations is not promised.

The order of stops makes an intriguing comparison possible: after Tiwanaku, you cross the border and explore Titicaca and Cusco on the Peruvian side. Pre-Inca stone architecture, lakeside traditions and later Inca monuments are experienced in sequence. For a cultural itinerary, it is worth leaving time for the guide to explain the distinctions between periods rather than letting the sites become one indistinguishable list of ruins.

Explore [other cultural and historical tours in Bolivia](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/bolivia/) if the Altiplano's monuments are your priority and you want fewer city flights.

## Lake Titicaca and the road from Puno to Cusco

After crossing the border, travellers reach the [Lake Titicaca area](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) and visit the [floating Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/) made of reeds. This introduces the lives and traditions of people living by the lake. It would be an exaggeration to claim that residents preserve every aspect of pre-Hispanic life unchanged or that the visit is a residential ethnographic expedition: it is a scheduled island excursion.

The following day features a group journey from Puno to Cusco by tourist bus. The itinerary lists stops at the church in Andahuaylillas, the archaeological complex of Raqchi, La Raya Pass and Pukará. Excursion stops make the drive part of the cultural experience, while lengthening the transfer. It is not a nonstop express journey.

[Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) was the capital of the Inca Empire, and the present city preserves both pre-Columbian and colonial structures. Tours include Qorikancha, Qenqo, Puka Pukara, Tambomachay and Sacsayhuamán. These sites connect religious, defensive and architectural aspects of Andean history. They are visited as part of the city excursion, so that day's schedule cannot be treated as entirely free time.

## Machu Picchu: a complete excursion day

[Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) has its own day on both journeys. The excursions are organised from Cusco in a group with an English-speaking guide; the return is by train. Lunch is included. This is a visit to the renowned Inca complex in a mountain setting, not an advertised multi-day trek on ancient trails.

UNESCO recognises both the cultural significance of Machu Picchu's stone architecture and its mountain setting. Access conditions, permitted visitor circuits and entry times depend on the actual tickets and site regulations. When planning, discuss not only the date but also the circuit within the complex, rail connections and time for the return journey.

If Cusco and Machu Picchu are your primary goals, compare [cultural tours in Peru](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/peru/). Both itineraries including Uruguay and Bolivia have many separate city and nature stages and require far more days.

## Montevideo: another chapter in South American history

[Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) appears on both itineraries as a ferry trip from Buenos Aires and back on the same day. A capital-city sightseeing tour follows arrival. The port, Independence Square, streets of the Old Town and cathedral introduce the coastal culture of the Río de la Plata.

The contrast with the Andean stage is striking: instead of pre-Columbian stone architecture, visitors encounter the city heritage of the Spanish colonial period, the emergence of independent states and contemporary capital life. This suits anyone interested in several distinct chapters of the continent's history. But a single day cannot cover all Uruguay's museums, theatres and smaller cities in detail.

The principal limitation is the ferry timetable. Departure and return times, boarding, port-to-centre transfers and border checks determine how much time remains for sightseeing. Add a museum or restaurant only after coordinating the schedule, rather than assuming it will fit because of a promotional description.

## Comparing the two available itineraries

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_latin_america_six_countries_20_days_2026,tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

The [20-day six-country journey](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) starts in Brazil, visits Argentina and Uruguay and continues through Chile and Bolivia into Peru. Its historical experiences are accompanied by Iguazu Falls, city sightseeing, jeep travel among Bolivian lagoons and Machu Picchu. It suits travellers wanting several historical traditions and natural regions in one trip with a relatively limited holiday period.

The [32-day eight-country journey](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) includes a similar historical sequence in Bolivia and Peru, but continues after Lima through Ecuador and Colombia. Quito, the Galápagos, Medellín, Cartagena and Bogotá add new cultural subjects, including colonial architecture and northern South American cities, alongside sea-based nature excursions.

The main reason to choose 32 days is the wider geography. It does not promise a longer stay at Tiwanaku or a two-day Machu Picchu excursion. For a deep cultural exploration specifically of Bolivia, Peru and Uruguay, discuss reallocating the days instead of automatically selecting the longest tour.

You can also explore [all multi-country cultural journeys](/multi-country/interests/culture-and-history/) and [general tours through Bolivia, Peru and Uruguay](/multi-country/bolivia_peru_uruguay/). The themed selection highlights cultural experiences; the general catalogue shows all current products with this geography.

## Time of year, altitude and practicalities

Altitude and weather provide the biggest contrast across these three countries. La Paz, Tiwanaku, Titicaca and Cusco are in the Andes, where exposed areas can be cold and windy even in bright sun. Montevideo is on the Atlantic coast and has different walking conditions. Pack for both: warm layers, comfortable shoes for stone pathways and sun protection at altitude, with lighter items for the city day.

The Bolivia section reaches over 4,000 metres. A tight schedule of archaeological visits does not remove the risk of altitude sickness: the rate of ascent and personal tolerance matter even for very fit travellers. Discuss medical concerns with a doctor before travelling. For a multi-week trip, consider sufficient sleep, flight buffers and potential timetable changes.

Border arrangements depend on nationality, flight routes and potential re-entry. Two important checkpoints are the Bolivia–Peru overland crossing and the round trip from Argentina to Uruguay. Ada Tours helps establish the actual sequence of borders, check documents for travellers' nationalities and coordinate connection times. Currencies and individual card acceptance also need checking separately in each country; no single payment method is guaranteed across the continent.

Choose the cultural priorities in advance. If archaeology matters most, allocate time to Tiwanaku, Cusco and Machu Picchu; if modern cities and independence-era history appeal more, consider longer stays in Buenos Aires and Montevideo. On a long fixed itinerary, adding such days changes the entire transport sequence.

## Frequently asked questions about history in Bolivia, Peru and Uruguay

### Can Tiwanaku and Machu Picchu be visited on the same journey?

Yes. Both feature on the 20-day and 32-day itineraries. Tiwanaku is visited on the route from La Paz to the Peruvian border, while Machu Picchu has its own excursion day from Cusco.

### Does Tiwanaku belong to the Inca civilisation?

Tiwanaku is associated with an earlier pre-Columbian Andean civilisation. Its culture differs from that of the Inca Empire and Cusco monuments. This contrast makes visiting both especially valuable for history enthusiasts.

### How long do travellers spend in Uruguay?

Both itineraries include one sightseeing day in Montevideo: a ferry from Buenos Aires, city tour and return to Argentina. A longer visit to Uruguay requires a different programme.

### Is there a hike to Machu Picchu?

The existing itineraries specify an excursion day with a train return, not a multi-day trek. The permitted circuit within the archaeological site must be agreed according to the ticket and visitor rules.

### Which tour is better for studying just these three countries?

Both have many of the same cultural stops within these countries. The 32-day itinerary extends the journey to Ecuador and Colombia. For more in-depth time at Tiwanaku, Cusco or Montevideo, a custom allocation of days makes more sense.

  Bolivia, Peru and Uruguay introduce three culinary traditions: Andean highland food, Peru's regional flavours and Uruguay's meat and wine culture. But travellers' interests must be distinguished from paid inclusions. The existing journey chiefly focuses on landmarks and nature; specialist tastings are not confirmed in these three countries, while an optional wine excursion is offered in Chile. Here is where gastronomy could be added and how much time it would take.
---

## Gastronomy on an extended itinerary: what is included and what needs arranging

The [20-day Six Latin American Countries tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) has substantial stages in Bolivia, Peru and Uruguay. Uruguay is a one-day excursion from Buenos Aires to Montevideo. Bolivia features the off-road journey through lagoons and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), then [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) and Tiwanaku. Peru covers Puno, the Andean road, [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and [Lima](/peru/place/lima/).

**This is an extensive sightseeing tour with a secondary interest in gastronomy, not a specialist three-country tasting tour.** The itinerary includes breakfasts and some lunches but no dedicated cooking class, wine tour or required tasting within Bolivia, Peru and Uruguay. An optional winery excursion in Chile's Maipo Valley, also on the six-country route, is available at additional cost.

The question before booking is therefore **where to add a standalone culinary experience without losing a scheduled excursion or flight**. The [Bolivia – Peru – Uruguay selection](/multi-country/bolivia_peru_uruguay/) shows the full border and transport sequence; here we focus on meals, markets, wine and the time available.

## Peru: the best place to allow a separate food-focused day

Among the three selected countries, Peru offers the broadest culinary possibilities within the geography of the existing tour. The route passes through [Puno](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), connecting highland foods with the Pacific coast. Peru's national tourism portal presents gastronomy as a reason to travel in its own right. In Lima, ceviche and tiradito are prominent, alongside cuisine shaped by local, African and Asian traditions.

However, the current itinerary uses Peru primarily for Lake Titicaca, Inca monuments and a Lima city tour. The tourist-bus ride from Puno to Cusco takes much of one day; Machu Picchu and other archaeological sites occupy separate excursions. Lima has a sightseeing day covering Miraflores and the historic centre. Fitting a full cooking workshop into every one of these days without revising the schedule would be a mistake.

**The most useful addition is dedicated time in Lima**, or a restaurant evening agreed in advance if the interval between tours and flights is sufficient. Choose the format according to your interests: tasting regional dishes, a guided food market visit, a cooking demonstration or a themed restaurant. Until an addition is confirmed, it remains a possible customisation rather than an included service.

In Cusco, food offers an opportunity to discuss Andean geography, regional produce and altitude. But visiting a community kitchen or farm should not be promised simply because the itinerary passes ancient settlements.

## Bolivia: meals on the high-altitude expedition stage

The Bolivian part differs greatly from a restaurant day in [Lima](/peru/place/lima/). After Chile, visitors cross the border, travel by jeep past lagoons and spend a night in expedition-style accommodation. A packed lunch is included on the second day. Uyuni follows, along with a flight to [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) and city sightseeing. The following day takes the group via Tiwanaku to the Peruvian border.

For travellers interested in food, the main consideration is the limited schedule. Elevations above 4,000 metres, road stops and accommodation far from large towns affect meals more than restaurant choice. Food during the drive is part of the logistics, **not a tasting programme**.

To discover Bolivian cuisine in more depth, discuss a separate meal or meeting with a local culinary expert in La Paz if the schedule permits. Arrival times, the city excursion and onward departure all need to be considered. Unconfirmed hours of free time should not be treated as a guaranteed food experience.

During acclimatisation, pay attention to drinking water, familiar foods and tolerance of physical exertion. Alcohol and very heavy meals immediately after rapid ascent can worsen wellbeing. If wine tasting and long restaurant dinners are your main priorities, low-altitude cities are preferable to the first evening on the highlands.

## Uruguay: Montevideo, parrilla and Tannat wine

Uruguay has a well-known tradition of charcoal-grilled meat and wines made with the Tannat grape. In [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/), the old port district has a thriving food scene; municipal sources highlight Mercado del Puerto for traditional food and restaurants. However, the [six-country tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) covers the harbour, Independence Square, the centre, [Old Town](/uruguay/place/montevideo-old-town/) and cathedral. Free time follows before the return ferry.

This is a genuine but **narrow window** to discover local food independently. A visit to Mercado del Puerto or a restaurant lunch is possible only if it fits the excursion timetable, avoids conflicts with the ferry and is agreed beforehand. Wineries outside the capital require more time and separate transport; the region's winemaking tradition does not mean a bodega visit is included in a day trip.

If you chiefly want to experience Uruguay as a wine country, consider an additional overnight stay or a different programme. On a short visit, focus on one culinary experience near the historic centre rather than attempting a full vineyard tour as well.

## Where wine is actually mentioned in the existing programme

The wine excursion on this route is in **Chile**. During sightseeing in [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), travellers can pay extra for a winery excursion to the Maipo Valley with a tasting. The wine excursion requires a minimum of two participants. **It is not automatically included in the base tour price.**

This explains why the gastronomic theme on the long six-country tour must be read alongside the actual itinerary. A page featuring three selected countries is a themed view of the whole journey, but the existence of a wine option in neighbouring Chile **does not turn into** a tasting in Bolivia, Peru or Uruguay.

| Country | Actual gastronomy status |
|---|---|
| Bolivia | Meals during travel; no tastings included |
| Peru | Cities with culinary possibilities; no specialist programme specified |
| Uruguay | Free time in Montevideo; winery not included |

For other wine destinations and journeys, see [Food and Wine travel](/interests/food-and-wine/) and [multi-country gastronomy tours](/multi-country/interests/food-and-wine/).

## Adding food and wine without disrupting the itinerary

Ada Tours can discuss tailored additions based on travel dates, group composition and available time: a Lima restaurant, a cultural and culinary experience in La Paz, time for Montevideo's local food or a confirmed winery excursion in Chile. Each proposal needs a separate check of duration and cost. None can be counted as included in the existing price until agreed.

For a multi-country journey, rules for carrying food and alcohol, hand-luggage restrictions and customs requirements at each border also matter. Check these against nationality, country of entry and travel date. Avoid buying perishable products at the start of a complicated route with long flights and land crossings. Different local currencies are used in the cities, so card acceptance and exchange options should be checked before departure.

If gastronomy is the principal aim rather than an extra interest, **allocate full days to it first**, then decide how many countries are practical. On a six-country sightseeing itinerary, that would be a deliberate redesign, not an invisible extra stop between two flights.

## Frequently asked questions about gastronomy in Bolivia, Peru and Uruguay

### Are culinary tastings included in all three countries?

No. Bolivia, Peru and Uruguay have sightseeing, nature and heritage sections on this itinerary, but no separate paid tastings are advertised in those three countries. A winery excursion is offered as an optional extra in Chile's Maipo Valley.

### Can I try Peruvian cuisine in Lima?

Lima offers excellent opportunities for food-focused travel, but the included excursion day already covers the city. Agree on a particular restaurant, market, tasting or cooking class separately and include it in a revised itinerary.

### Is there enough free time in Montevideo for a winery?

The one-day visit includes sightseeing and a return ferry to Buenos Aires. A proper winery trip generally requires additional time and transport. Consider changing the Uruguay stage instead of assuming it is included.

### Why does a gastronomy theme apply to these three countries if the wine is in Chile?

Because the [20-day tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) visits six countries and its thematic classification applies to the entire journey. This page shows the tour passing through Bolivia, Peru and Uruguay, while the wine option is located on the Chilean stage.

lead: >-
  Bolivia's colourful lagoons and Uyuni Salt Flat lead into Peru's high-altitude Lake Titicaca, La Raya Pass and Machu Picchu. Uruguay is represented by a day in Montevideo on these same journeys. Here is the actual order of the highland stages and how the 20-day and 32-day programmes differ.
---

## Bolivia, Peru and Uruguay: what the nature itinerary looks like

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. Both programmes include [Bolivia](/bolivia/), [Peru](/peru/) and [Uruguay](/uruguay/) as principal countries, but the nature experiences are not divided into three equal sections. **Bolivia and Peru are joined by a continuous journey through the Andes**, while Uruguay is a short sightseeing stop elsewhere in the itinerary.

The two options, [Six Latin American Countries in 20 Days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) and [Eight South American Countries in 32 Days](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), both travel from San Pedro de Atacama via Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons, [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), La Paz, Lake Titicaca and Cusco to Machu Picchu. These stages are similar on both programmes; the longer tour then continues through Ecuador and Colombia.

## Bolivia: colourful lakes, geysers and a salt plain

After Chile's Atacama, the itinerary begins a 4×4 highland route through Bolivia with an English-speaking guide. The first day includes [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), Salvador Dalí Desert, Polques hot springs, [Sol de Mañana geysers](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/) and [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). One drive reveals greenish and reddish waters, mineral landscapes and active geothermal features.

The next day crosses Honda, Chiar Khota, Hedionda and Cañapa lagoons and the Ollagüe and Chiguana areas towards Uyuni. Stops at Colchani and on the salt flat are included. Nature is experienced through a series of short visits during lengthy drives. Neither a separate volcano ascent nor a multi-day walking trail is listed for these days.

A flight from Uyuni to La Paz follows. The high-altitude city stage also prepares for the journey to Peru, via Tiwanaku and the Desaguadero border area. It is a transition from dry plateau landscapes to the Lake Titicaca highland ecosystem.

## Peru: Titicaca, La Raya and Machu Picchu's mountains

After crossing the border, travellers arrive in the [Puno and Lake Titicaca area](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). An afternoon trip to the reed-built Uros Islands is scheduled. This offers a chance to experience a high-altitude body of water and discover the lives of people whose traditions are closely tied to the lake. It is a combined cultural and nature visit, not a wildlife safari.

The next day, the group travels to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) by tourist bus. Stops include Andahuaylillas, Raqchi, [La Raya Pass](/peru/place/la-raya-pass/) and Pukará, with lunch in Sicuani. The principal nature experience is the road through open Andean slopes and valleys. The guided bus journey with scheduled stops is different from free trekking in the mountains.

A separate excursion visits [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). Inca stone terraces and buildings sit among steep green mountains. The transition from open highland plateau to wetter valleys is visible in the vegetation too. Both itineraries specify a group excursion with an English-speaking guide and return travel to Cusco by train. **The Inca Trail trek is not included in this day.**

## Uruguay: a ferry and a walk through Montevideo

Uruguay appears much earlier than the Bolivia–Peru highland stages. Travellers take a ferry from Buenos Aires across the Río de la Plata to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/), tour the port and historic centre and return to Argentina the same day. Ferry tickets are included on both programmes.

The crossing offers water and shoreline views, but the excursion itself is a city tour. **The route does not include a separate Uruguay nature-park visit, an overnight stay on the ocean coast or a multi-day water expedition.** For travellers whose sole aim is the Andes, this stop is useful mainly as part of a wider culture-and-nature journey.

The itinerary therefore cannot be read as “Montevideo → Uyuni → Titicaca”. Chile lies between Uruguay and Bolivia, while both tours begin with Brazil and Argentina.

## Why the high-altitude section is demanding

Bolivia involves 4×4 travel, the Puno–Cusco leg is by tourist bus and the Machu Picchu excursion includes a railway segment. These are three different transport modes within a short part of the journey. Elevation, dry air and temperature swings require warm clothing and sun protection together; long travel days require tolerance for lengthy journeys.

Both itineraries include acclimatisation time in San Pedro de Atacama before Bolivia. That makes the transition more gradual but cannot remove every risk of altitude illness. Discuss your health and tolerance of high elevations with a doctor before travelling, especially with chronic conditions. The route and means of transport should be reviewed with your travel manager in advance.

### Can I see Uyuni and Machu Picchu on one journey?

Yes. Both tours visit Uyuni, then continue via La Paz, Puno and Cusco to Machu Picchu. The journey involves road travel and a flight, not one direct transfer.

### Which tour should I choose for the Andes?

## Laguna Colorada flamingos: the principal wildlife stop

Both tours travel through the highlands of southwestern [Bolivia](/bolivia/). The most specific wildlife-watching stop is [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). Eduardo Avaroa Andean Fauna National Reserve is home to different flamingo species, including James's flamingo. The birds move freely, and their numbers and locations near the shore depend on the season and lake conditions.

The programme includes off-road travel past high-altitude lagoons, desert landscapes, Chiguana Salt Flat and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). The salt flat is primarily a landscape attraction, while the lagoons offer better prospects for seeing birds. Nobody can guarantee a particular species, flock size or close-range photograph.

The tour operates at high altitude, with lengthy road journeys and early starts. Sunshine, wind and cold can occur together. Binoculars are helpful, while a telephoto lens and dust protection are useful for photography. Observe protected-area rules and do not approach the birds for a shot.

## Peru: Lake Titicaca and the Uros Islands

In [Peru](/peru/), the route passes [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). Its reedbeds and wetlands provide habitats for waterbirds and are protected in the Titicaca National Reserve. However, the main scheduled excursion visits the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/) and introduces the culture of communities that build structures from reeds.

Visitors may see nature during the boat crossing, but specialist birdwatching or a dedicated ornithological expedition is not part of the paid excursions. If your goal is to watch birds for several hours, the route and guidance must be arranged separately.

After Titicaca, the group visits [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and Lima. These are chiefly cultural and historical days. For more time in nature, compare [Peru tours under the Nature theme](/interests/nature/tours/peru/) by duration and activities.

## Uruguay: a city day without a nature safari

[Uruguay](/uruguay/) is visited on both itineraries by ferry from Buenos Aires to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/). City sightseeing includes the [Old Town](/uruguay/place/montevideo-old-town/), [Independence Square](/uruguay/place/montevideo-independence-square/), [port](/uruguay/place/montevideo-port/) and other stops. Travellers return to Argentina in the evening.

No nature reserve, marine safari or dedicated birdwatching excursion is scheduled for this day. The visit introduces the city and the Río de la Plata waterfront. Uruguay's natural areas would require a separate itinerary with more time.

## 20 or 32 days: how wildlife opportunities differ

The journey from Brazil's waterfalls through Montevideo, Chile, Bolivia's lagoons and Titicaca is similar on both programmes. **The 20-day tour** ends in Lima, combining Altiplano flamingos with Andean culture and capital-city excursions.

**The 32-day tour** continues from Peru through Ecuador and Colombia. Ecuador includes the Galápagos Islands and nature excursions with opportunities to observe island wildlife. This is a major addition for travellers who value animals more than urban sightseeing. However, the Galápagos lie *outside* the three selected countries and require a much longer journey.

## Preparing for different climates and borders

The journey combines humid tropical areas, the coast and cold highlands. Pack layers, wind and rain protection, comfortable footwear, sunscreen and protection for camera equipment. Discuss any medical limitations and allow suitable acclimatisation time before the high-altitude stage.

The route includes returning from Uruguay to Argentina, a flight to Chile, the land crossing into Bolivia and entry to Peru. Visa and transit rules, permitted numbers of entries and document validity depend on nationality and the actual route. We help coordinate the necessary checks and sensible connection times. Entry permission is determined by each country's official requirements.

## Frequently asked questions about wildlife in Bolivia, Peru and Uruguay

### Where might we see flamingos on these tours?

In the Bolivian highlands, particularly at [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). Wild-bird sightings depend on the season and conditions at the site.

### Is birdwatching included on Lake Titicaca?

No. The programme includes a visit to the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/). Extended specialist birdwatching would require additional arrangements.

### Is there a safari in Uruguay?

No. Montevideo has a sightseeing excursion as part of a one-day visit from Argentina.

### Which tour should I choose for animals?

If you chiefly want to see Bolivia's lagoons, both routes provide them. If you also want the Galápagos, choose the [32-day tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/): that Ecuador nature stage is only included on the longer itinerary.
